title: Propagate attachment read and encoding errors
description:
Attachment::base64_data currently turns get_data failures into empty data via unwrap_or_default. This can deliver corrupted emails with empty attachments while returning Ok. Make attachment serialization fallible and propagate MailError through every provider path.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create an Attachment with from_path_lazy pointing at a file.
2. Delete the file or make it unreadable before delivery.
3. Send through a provider that serializes attachments with base64_data.
4. Observe that the attachment content becomes empty instead of returning an error to the caller.
acceptance_criteria: Missing or unreadable lazy attachments cause delivery to fail; provider code propagates the original MailError; regression tests cover missing file and permission/read failure behavior.

title: Preserve source error chains in MailError
description: MailError currently derives Clone and stringifies underlying errors such as reqwest, lettre, serde_json, and IO errors. Redesign errors to preserve source chains for downstream diagnostics, retry classification, and observability.
acceptance_criteria: MailError variants store source errors where useful; std::error::Error::source exposes causal chains; Clone is removed unless there is a clear replacement strategy; provider tests assert useful error classification.

title: Introduce validated email preparation model
description: Validation is currently split between deliver wrappers and provider adapters, and direct Mailer::deliver calls can behave differently. Define a clear validation/preparation boundary, such as EmailDraft to PreparedEmail, so provider implementations receive a consistently valid message.
acceptance_criteria: Provider adapters receive a prepared/validated email type or shared validation path; direct provider use cannot bypass required validation accidentally; tests cover global/client/direct-mailer send paths.

title: Encapsulate public Email, Address, and Attachment fields
description: Core data structs expose representation directly, making invalid states easy and future refactors semver-breaking. Move toward private fields, accessors, and constructors/builders that preserve flexibility without freezing internals.
acceptance_criteria: Core struct fields are private or intentionally minimized; public getters/builders cover common use; serde compatibility and migration impact are documented.

title: Replace stringly provider_options with typed provider option APIs
description: Email::provider_options uses HashMap<String, serde_json::Value> for provider-specific behavior, which makes typos and type errors runtime-only. Add typed option APIs for provider-specific capabilities and keep a clearly marked raw escape hatch only where necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Common provider features like Resend scheduled_at/idempotency/tags have typed APIs; invalid option types fail at compile time or validation; raw JSON option use is documented as advanced escape hatch.

title: Replace core env auto-detection with explicit typed configuration
description: Environment variable probing is currently embedded in core delivery flow. Refactor toward explicit configuration structs and a from_env helper so env behavior is opt-in and testable rather than hidden global behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Provider config types validate required fields; from_env is isolated and testable; primary send path does not read process env; auto-detection order is documented or removed.

title: Introduce instance-based EmailClient as the primary API
description: Move the architectural center from global deliver() to an explicit EmailClient configured by the application. Consumers should construct a client from typed config or a concrete provider and pass it through app state/dependency injection.
acceptance_criteria: Docs and examples use EmailClient first; EmailClient can send single and batch emails; global deliver remains only as an optional convenience or compatibility facade.

title: Remove PII from default telemetry
description:
deliver and deliver_with include recipient addresses and subject lines in info-level tracing spans. Library defaults should not emit email addresses or subjects to normal logs because consumers may forward logs to third-party observability systems.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install an info-level tracing subscriber in a consumer application.
2. Call missive::deliver or missive::deliver_with with a real recipient and subject.
3. Observe recipient addresses and subject text attached to the info-level missive.deliver span.
acceptance_criteria: Info-level spans/logs include provider, status, counts, and timing only; subject/address logging requires debug/trace or explicit opt-in; tests or snapshot assertions cover span fields where practical.

title: Audit provider attachment handling for lazy data support
description:
Provider adapters handle attachments inconsistently. SMTP uses attachment.data directly, which bypasses lazy file loading, while API providers call base64_data. Audit all providers so eager and lazy attachments behave consistently and fail consistently.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create an Email with a lazy path-based attachment.
2. Send it through SMTP and at least one HTTP provider test double.
3. Compare payloads and failure behavior.
4. Observe that providers do not consistently load lazy data or propagate lazy-read failures.
acceptance_criteria: Every provider either supports lazy attachments correctly or returns UnsupportedFeature; tests cover SMTP and at least one HTTP provider with lazy attachments.

title: Decide target public API shape for v0.7
description:
Choose the target architecture before large breaking edits. Evaluate an instance-oriented EmailClient API, typed provider configuration, whether globals remain behind an optional facade, and how provider dispatch should work for both static and dynamic use cases.

## Rationale
The remaining v0.7 cleanup tasks are coupled. Public field encapsulation, env handling, provider options, validation, and dynamic dispatch all depend on the desired public API shape. A decision record should prevent incompatible partial refactors.

## Alternatives Considered
- Keep global deliver as the primary API and harden internals only.
- Make EmailClient with typed config the primary API and keep globals as optional compatibility sugar.
- Split static generic clients from boxed dynamic clients.
- Defer breaking changes and patch only correctness bugs.
acceptance_criteria: Decision records preferred primary API, global-facade policy, provider dispatch strategy, and migration constraints.

title: Refactor missive toward an idiomatic Rust library API
description: Track the v0.7-style cleanup needed to make missive feel like a high-quality Rust library rather than an app-style/global facade. This covers explicit client configuration, typed provider options, safer data models, attachment correctness, telemetry defaults, error sources, and migration documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Primary library API is instance-based; correctness bugs are fixed; breaking changes have migration guidance; remaining global helpers are clearly optional convenience APIs.

title: Write migration guide for breaking v0.7 library API changes
description: The cleanup will likely require breaking API changes. Document migration from global deliver/env setup to EmailClient/config, typed provider options, private fields/builders, and updated attachment/error behavior.
acceptance_criteria: README and docs include old-to-new examples; breaking changes are listed with rationale; CHANGELOG has a migration section.

title: Audit address formatting and header support across providers
description: Some provider adapters use Address::formatted rather than RFC5322-safe formatting, and SMTP currently ignores custom headers. Audit provider-specific expectations for names, IDNs, reply-to behavior, and custom headers to prevent malformed messages or silently dropped fields.
acceptance_criteria: Provider address formatting is consistent and documented; tests cover display names with quotes/commas and IDN domains; unsupported custom headers fail or are documented instead of silently ignored.

title: Evaluate native async trait API versus boxed Mailer adapter
description:
The current Mailer trait uses async_trait to support dyn Mailer. Decide whether the redesigned primary API should use native async fn in traits for static dispatch, a boxed object-safe adapter for runtime dispatch, or keep async_trait for pragmatic compatibility.

## Rationale
Native async functions in traits reduce boxing for static dispatch, but they are not object-safe. Missive currently relies on Arc<dyn Mailer> for runtime provider selection, so changing this affects the entire provider and client architecture.

## Alternatives Considered
- Keep async_trait everywhere for object-safe simplicity.
- Use native async fn in the primary trait and provide a separate boxed adapter.
- Avoid a public async trait and make EmailClient own provider enums/config directly.
- Delay this choice until after EmailClient design is settled.
acceptance_criteria: Decision explains object-safety tradeoff, dispatch modes, migration cost, and recommended public trait/API shape.

title: Reduce Email cloning and attachment memory amplification
description: prepare_email, interceptors, local storage, and provider conversion paths clone Email values. Large Vec<u8> attachments can be copied repeatedly. Audit clone paths and shift large attachment data to bytes::Bytes, Arc<[u8]>, or consuming APIs where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Large attachment data is not duplicated by routine Email clones; benchmarks or targeted tests demonstrate lower clone cost; API ownership model is documented.

title: Move lazy attachment file reads off async worker threads
description: Lazy attachment reads use std::fs::read in delivery paths. For async runtimes, large or slow file reads should use tokio::fs or spawn_blocking so send operations do not block executor worker threads.
acceptance_criteria: Lazy attachment file reads are async-runtime friendly; implementation works without forcing Tokio on non-Tokio users or clearly gates runtime-specific behavior; tests cover lazy file sends.

title: Remove global LocalMailer storage coupling
description: local_storage() uses a process-global OnceLock for preview integration. Refactor preview/local mailer setup so applications pass an explicit MemoryStorage instance to LocalMailer and the preview UI, enabling isolated concurrent sandboxes and tests.
acceptance_criteria: Preview examples use explicit storage wiring; multiple independent local mailboxes can coexist in one process; local_storage global is removed, deprecated, or isolated behind compatibility facade.

title: Audit docs for stale versions and feature-bundle accuracy
description: Documentation has version drift and bundle descriptions that may not exactly match Cargo features. Audit README and docs so examples, versions, and feature bundle descriptions match Cargo.toml.
acceptance_criteria: README/docs versions match crate version policy; feature bundle descriptions match Cargo.toml; preview docs no longer reference stale versions.
